title: Choose the visual world for Spaces
question: The roll assigned the Card Catalog. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Card Catalog
options.lineage: Library Bureau steel card cabinets and typed 3×5 catalog cards
options.thesis: Every Space is an index card in one drawer: this window's Space is the card pulled up and read, the rest are card tops you flick to.
materials: white card stock with faint blue rules
options.viewport: The pulled card fills the top: typed Space name, call number (its 1–9 shortcut), tab entries with hanging indents and group headings; below it, a dense stack of card tops, one line each, filed under workspace guide cards.
options.risk: Turns into costume if the card is decoration instead of structure; typed faces read slower at small sizes, so entries need a careful size floor.

raised.raise: Red is spent on one thing only: the current card's top rule and the act of pulling (switching).
Every state is a distinct stamped mark in a fixed cell: HERE, OPEN, a device name, PENDING, VIEW ONLY.
Rank is one variable: how far a card is pulled out of the drawer; no shadows, badges or boxes to fake importance.
Absence is designed: empty drawers, zero tabs and offline states are drawn as blank cards with typed notes, not grey placeholders.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: European railway platform signage and departure boards
options.thesis: The window is your platform: the Space standing at it is signed large, and every other Space is a departure you can board.
options.viewport: A dark platform sign carries the current Space name at display size; a departures table lists the others with tab counts and status, keyboard-numbered like platforms.
options.risk: The most familiar direction on this list (timetables are a common switching metaphor), and a dark sign beside every page is heavy in daylight.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size for everything: rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule, with Spaces as departure rows.
options.viewport: A single-size timetable: the current Space is the one reversed plate, the rest are departure rows with state marks in fixed cells.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (Spaces as departures) and wins on density, but a lit goldenrod bed beside every page all day is the loudness you ruled out.
options.risk: Raked containers and a saturated bed fight a narrow panel that has to sit quietly next to real work.

options.label: Festival Lineup
options.thesis: Billing is the whole hierarchy: the Space you're in is the headliner across the full width, the rest shrink into a justified block.
options.viewport: The current Space name spans the panel at headliner size; other Spaces step down by recency into a dense justified block you click or type into.
options.case: Unbeatable at 'which Space am I in', but a saturated full-panel ground competes with the page you're working on.
options.risk: Loud by construction; muting the ground would kill what makes it work.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One gold cord pulls a flat plane into shape.
options.viewport: A black field where one control reshapes the view.
options.case: Nothing in switching tabs is a garment; the metaphor never becomes function.
options.kept: One accent reserved for the one action.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Forces made visible as rods and red cord.
options.viewport: A force diagram of Spaces and devices.
options.case: A diagram of forces obscures a simple list you switch through dozens of times a day.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Rank as depth on a black void, nothing enclosed.
options.viewport: A still front line of text over drifting layers.
options.case: Reads as a dev toy beside real work, and drifting motion all day is a distraction.
options.risk: Loud and technical, both ruled out.
options.kept: Rank carried by a single variable.

options.label: Seven-Segment
options.thesis: One segment mask, unlit cells designed too.
options.case: Great for numbers, useless for Space names and tab titles.
options.kept: Absence drawn as deliberately as presence.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean native-feeling sidebar list, as Workona or Arc would ship it, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Current Space as a highlighted row at the top, a searchable list below, tabs for resources and settings.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tab manager by design.
